items.stem: Define the term 'management'.
items.answer: Getting things done through other people by planning, organising, commanding, coordinating and controlling resources.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – Getting things done through other people by planning, organising, commanding, coordinating and controlling resources. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain two of Fayol's functions of management.
items.answer: Planning: setting objectives and deciding how to achieve them; controlling: measuring performance against plans and taking corrective action.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark function, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Explain how Mintzberg's view of management differs from Fayol's.
items.answer: Fayol describes what managers should do in a logical sequence; Mintzberg observed what managers actually do – a variety of interpersonal, informational and decisional roles carried out in short, fragmented activities.
items.markingKey: 1 mark Fayol prescriptive functions; 1 mark Mintzberg observed roles; 1 mark example. [3]

items.stem: Café Cordillera is a private limited company in Bogotá, Colombia with about 900 staff. It roasts coffee and runs a chain of 60 cafés. The owners want to double the number of cafés within three years. Explain how the managers of Café Cordillera could use Fayol's functions of management when launching bottled cold-brew coffee for supermarkets.
items.answer: Points to develop for Café Cordillera: Fayol's functions: planning, organising, commanding, coordinating, controlling; planning objectives and resources for the launch; organising and coordinating departments; controlling progress against targets.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: Fayol's functions: planning, organising, commanding, coordinating, controlling. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Café Cordillera (food and drink retail). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. planning objectives and resources for the launch; organising and coordinating departments. [3]

items.answer: Points to develop for BatikPay: Fayol's functions: planning, organising, commanding, coordinating, controlling; planning objectives and resources for the launch; organising and coordinating departments; controlling progress against targets.

AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. planning objectives and resources for the launch; organising and coordinating departments. [3]

items.stem: Savanna Fresh is a private limited company in Nairobi, Kenya with about 850 staff. It grows cut flowers and green beans and exports them by air to supermarkets in Europe. Its largest European customer has just demanded lower prices and proof of sustainable water use. Evaluate whether Mintzberg's roles are more useful than Fayol's functions in explaining the work of managers at Savanna Fresh.
items.answer: For: Mintzberg reflects what managers actually do; covers interpersonal and information roles; suits fast-changing businesses. Against: Fayol gives a clear framework; planning and control remain essential; both are generalisations. Judgement: for Savanna Fresh it depends mainly on the level of the manager, and also on the nature of the business.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts. AO2 Application [2]: uses the evidence (Savanna Fresh: horticulture, about 850 employees, private limited company in Kenya; its largest European customer has just demanded lower prices and proof of sustainable water use). AO3 Analysis [3]: arguments for, e.g. Mintzberg reflects what managers actually do; covers interpersonal and information roles; suits fast-changing businesses; arguments against, e.g. Fayol gives a clear framework; planning and control remain essential; both are generalisations. AO4 Evaluation [3]: a justified judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the level of the manager; the nature of the business; how fast its environment changes. A top-level answer reaches a supported conclusion specific to Savanna Fresh. [10]

items.stem: Define the term 'autocratic leadership'.
items.answer: A style in which the leader makes decisions alone and tells employees what to do, with little consultation.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – A style in which the leader makes decisions alone and tells employees what to do, with little consultation. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of democratic leadership.
items.answer: Advantage: employees feel valued and contribute ideas, raising motivation and the quality of decisions. Disadvantage: decisions take longer because of consultation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark advantage, 1 mark explanation; 1 mark disadvantage, 1 mark explanation. [4]

items.stem: Explain why no single leadership style is best in all situations.
items.answer: The best style depends on the task, the urgency of the decision and the skills and attitudes of the employees: autocratic suits crises, democratic suits skilled teams.
items.markingKey: 1 mark depends on situation; 1 mark example; 1 mark second example. [3]

items.stem: Indus Sports is a private limited company in Karachi, Pakistan with about 950 staff. It makes hand-stitched and machine-stitched footballs and cricket equipment. A rival in China has started selling machine-made balls at lower prices. Explain the effects on employees of Indus Sports if the new managing director adopts an autocratic style.
items.answer: Points to develop for Indus Sports: autocratic leaders decide without consultation; faster decisions and clear instructions; lower motivation as ideas are ignored; possible increase in labour turnover.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: autocratic leaders decide without consultation. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Indus Sports (sports equipment manufacturing). items.stem: Define the term 'Theory X'.
items.answer: McGregor's view that managers assume workers dislike work, avoid responsibility and must be controlled and motivated mainly by pay.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – McGregor's view that managers assume workers dislike work, avoid responsibility and must be controlled and motivated mainly by pay. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain how a manager's view of workers could affect the leadership style used.
items.answer: A Theory X manager is likely to be autocratic and supervise closely; a Theory Y manager is likely to be democratic and delegate.
items.markingKey: 1 mark Theory X → autocratic; 1 mark Theory Y → democratic/delegation. [2]

items.stem: Explain why Theory X assumptions could become a self-fulfilling prophecy.
items.answer: If workers are treated as lazy, closely controlled and given no responsibility, they become demotivated and behave in the way the manager expected.
items.markingKey: 1 mark close control; 1 mark demotivation; 1 mark behaviour confirms assumption. [3]

items.stem: Define the term 'emotional intelligence'.
items.answer: The ability of a person to understand and manage their own emotions and to recognise and influence the emotions of others.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – The ability of a person to understand and manage their own emotions and to recognise and influence the emotions of others. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why emotional intelligence is important for a manager.
items.answer: Managers work through people; understanding their own and others' emotions helps them communicate, resolve conflict and motivate staff.
